204 AM EST Sat Nov 28 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Water levels in the Bay and Potomac continue to decrease.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Snow showers and freezing drizzle continue in the
  Alleghenies through daybreak.

- 2) A cold front brings back precipitation & gusty winds 
  Sunday night into Monday, followed by drier conditions early 
  next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Snow showers and freezing drizzle continue in
the Alleghenies overnight. 

Cameras continue to show snow showers with some freezing drizzle
across the Alleghenies. This will continue through about sunrise
as moisture slowly erodes. Elsewhere, mostly cloudy skies are 
expected overnight, with overnight lows in the 30s to lower 40s.

Residual clouds should tend to break up over the course of the 
day, leading to a fair amount of sunshine by this afternoon. 
Winds will be gusty out of the west, but temperatures will run a
bit warmer, with highs in the mid to upper 50s for most 
(30s/40s mountains).

KEY MESSAGE 2...A cold front brings back precipitation & gusty 
winds Sunday night into Monday, followed by drier conditions early 
next week. 

High pressure will keep the region dry Sunday. Temperatures will be 
near seasonable with highs middle 50s to lower 60s. 

Shortwave upper-level ridging slides offshore late Sunday as a deep 
upper-level trough forms over the Midwest before tracking through 
the Mid-Atlantic late Sunday & into Monday. This will produce a 
strong cold front that will bring back the chance for areawide rain 
showers as well as wintry precipitation across the Alleghenies 
beginning Sunday night through Monday morning. Total QPF at this 
time ranges between 0.25"-0.75" as it quickly traverses the region. 
As the low tracks offshore Monday, winds will again become gusty 
creating blustery conditions, possibly gusting up to 35-40 knots at 
times. These should quickly diminish starting late Monday & into 
Tuesday as the low quickly transitions offshore, with temperatures 
falling a bit in the wake of the cold front. Afternoon highs on 
Tuesday fall to the 40s to low-50s, with overnight lows largely 
ranging in the 20s to low-30s. 

Looking towards the rest of the week, surface high pressure 
transitions in overhead with zonal flow reigning in the upper 
levels. This should bring drier & calmer conditions to the region, 
with southerly winds generally remaining light and temperatures 
gradually increasing back into the upper 50s as the week goes
on.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions are forecast over the next several 
days, although there could be a brief period before daybreak of
MVFR CIGs. Winds pick up again after sunrise with daytime 
mixing with gusts to around 20-25 kt expected. Winds become 
lighter on Sunday as high pressure builds traverses the area, 
but turn from a southerly direction. Showers are expected Sunday
night.

Winds become gusty again Monday in the wake of a powerful cold 
front, gusting up to 35-40 knots at times flowing northwesterly. 
Rain showers may linger into Monday morning, but conditions return 
to VFR by Monday afternoon and remain dry through midweek. Winds 
quickly diminish by Tuesday, with light winds generally flowing 
southerly by Wednesday. 

&&

.MARINE...
All Gale Warnings have been dropped as winds continue to
diminish. However, SCA conditions will continue through
Saturday with gusts up to 25 kt expected. 

An area of low pressure will move NW hrough the region late Sunday & 
into Monday, bringing areawide rain showers. Gale-force winds are 
possible with this system before diminishing by Tuesday. Light winds 
shift southerly by Wednesday. 

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies continue to decrease this evening. This
evening's tide cycle is expected to be the final one with
coastal flooding issues as anomalies continue to drop rapidly 
through the day Saturday.

&&
